The Electrical Reliability Engineer is responsible for coordinating the planning, organizing, and completion of mill reliability programs within the area of assigned responsibility. The engineer will help to define and participate in the development of electrical reliability programs to improve maintain and improve reliability of electrical machinery in the mill. This includes providing technical direction, assistance, and solutions to maintenance and operating personnel.

Responsible for managing all phases of developing key maintenance programs from conception through final implementation.
Will work with key maintenance and engineering personnel to support daily, monthly scheduled maintenance outages and annual outages jobs within the field of electrical maintenance and engineering. 
Some crossover activities to the mechanical maintenance programs will be required to deliver complete programs for all types of equipment. 
Will work with mechanical maintenance/engineering and operations personnel to complete electrical or mechanical maintenance projects and programs including: necessary training, stocking of spare parts, preventive maintenance checklists, drawing creation and updates, etc. 
Supports the Mills goals for safety, environmental, and other areas of need.
Focus on electrical equipment reliability.
Manage equipment tracking and rebuild programs.
Utilize predictive & preventative maintenance programs to identify and correct equipment issues.
Input and update equipment information and documentation.
Develop equipment manuals for precision inspection and maintenance of equipment.
Manage area equipment PM and maintenance programs.
Manage assigned work for monthly and annual outages.
Assist with MS Project timelines for monthly an annual outages.
Plan and execute capital projects for maintenance replacements of equipment.
Effectively manage jobs for best result at lowest cost.
Look for opportunities to solve issues, reduce cost, and improve planning performance.
Solve problems utilizing the mill’s RCFA program.
Effectively manages contractors for performing jobs.
Performs other responsibilities as needed.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering or equivalent education and experience required.
A minimum of 2-5 years’ experience, or the equivalent, in Electrical maintenance.
Experience using Microsoft Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, Project, and AutoCAD. 
Successful completion of drug screen required and authorization to work in the U.S.
Preferred Qualifications
Pulp & Paper industry experience preferred.
 
The successful candidate must possess the following Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:
Ability to be able to work well under pressure and within time constraints, multitask, and build sound relationships with both internal and external customers 
Ability to exhibit excellent communication, analytical, organizational, and computer skills. 
Capable of independently making sound decisions through creative problem-solving, ambiguity, and change.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple requests simultaneously.
Ability to read and understand technical correspondence, memos, instructions, and reports.
Ability to apply skills to continuous process improvement while maintaining maximum levels of safety.
Demonstrated leadership skills and abilities. 
Strong planning and follow-up skills. 
Excellent people and process management skills.

jobPostings.jobDescription:
Electrical Engineering Co Op/Intern
We are seeking resumes for an electrical engineering co-op. This application may lead to three potential job titles depending on mill needs: an electrical reliability engineering co-op, an electrical project engineering co-op, or a process control engineering co-op. The primary responsibilities of each are detailed below.
Electrical Reliability Engineering Co-Op

Support electrical reliability assignments that improve mill safety, equipment performance, operational efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
Work with reliability engineers, maintenance, operations, and mill personnel to troubleshoot electrical and equipment reliability issues.
Apply predictive and preventive maintenance techniques to improve equipment reliability and support root-cause failure analyses.
Assist with special reliability projects and additional assignments that support safe, efficient, and reliable mill operations.
Additional duties as requested by management.

Electrical Project Engineering Co-Op

Support electrical project engineering assignments involving planning, design, installation, commissioning, and startup of mill electrical equipment.
Assist with electrical equipment projects, including motors, MCCs, lighting, valves, switches, sensors, cameras, instrumentation, and related systems.
Use AutoCAD, P&ID drawings, process information systems, Trident, Microsoft Office, and other company software to update drawings, create new project documentation, and maintain equipment files.
Coordinate with project engineers, operations, contractors, maintenance shops, and other disciplines to support safe project execution, installation, and startup.
Support project management activities such as scope development, schedule coordination, cost tracking, contractor oversight, and communication with mill personnel.
Additional duties as requested by management.

Process Control Engineering Co-Op

Support process control engineers, instrument technicians, and mill operations with troubleshooting, advanced process control, DCS, and control system improvement efforts.
Use process information systems, Microsoft Office, Trident, AutoCAD, and other company software to update drawings, equipment files, functional specifications, and control documentation.
Assist with system audits, loop checks, I/O checkout, startup support, and correction of control system documentation and wiring records during outages or down days.
Collect, enter, and analyze process and control systems data to support troubleshooting, reliability, process optimization, and business decision-making.
Additional duties as requested by management.

 
Basic Qualifications:
Required:
A minimum grade point average of 3.0/4.0 is required and must be a permanent U.S. resident with a valid driver’s license. Must be majoring in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology or a related field and have completed freshman year or will have completed freshman year at time of co-op or internship. 
Preferred:
Currently a member of the paper foundation at the following schools: Auburn University, Georgia Tech University, University of Maine, Miami University (Ohio), University of Minnesota – Twin Cities, NC State University, SUNY ESF, University of Washington – Seattle, Western Michigan University, University of Wisconsin – Stevens Point, or currently enrolled at any State University or Technological University in the following states: AL, FL, GA, IL, ID, LA, MI, MN, MS, NC, ND, OH, TN, TX, VA, WA, WI. Students that sign up for interviews during the Career Fairs and On-Campus Interview days at the schools listed will be given first consideration.
Completing this application makes you eligible for consideration at any of PCA’s 10 mill locations as follows:

Counce, TN 
Deridder, LA

Responsibilities
Provide technical and operating support to departments, support groups, and hourly operations employees in the areas of optimization, energy and cost savings, technical and process studies, technology implementation and operator training. Assignments will include completion of projects and development activities to prepare for operation and maintenance positions as vacancies occur. Assignments are made to enhance skill development while gaining orientation of various process areas.
Qualifications
BS Degree in engineering required (Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical or Paper Science). Co-op or Intern experience in a manufacturing environment is a plus. Must be willing and able to work any shift, weekends, holidays, and overtime, as needed.

Position Summary:  As a Reliability Engineer at our paper mill facility, you will be responsible for ensuring the effective maintenance, repair, and optimization of mechanical equipment critical to the paper production process. You will utilize your expertise in mechanical engineering and maintenance principles to maximize equipment reliability, minimize downtime, and support the overall operational efficiency of the mill.
Principle Accountabilities:  

Plan, schedule, and coordinate mechanical maintenance activities to ensure the uninterrupted operation of papermaking equipment, including but not limited to pumps, conveyors, boilers, turbines, and associated systems.
Lead troubleshooting efforts to diagnose and resolve complex mechanical issues, utilizing root cause analysis techniques to identify underlying problems and implement effective solutions.
Develop and implement preventive maintenance programs tailored to specific equipment and processes, incorporating reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) principles to optimize maintenance strategies and extend equipment lifespan.
Oversee the execution of maintenance tasks, including routine inspections, lubrication, alignment, and component replacement, ensuring compliance with safety protocols, manufacturer guidelines, and engineering standards.
Utilize computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) to manage work orders, track equipment history, and analyze maintenance data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including operations, reliability engineering, and procurement, to support equipment upgrades, modifications, and reliability improvement initiatives.
Participate in the selection, installation, commissioning, and acceptance testing of new equipment and upgrades, providing input on design considerations, maintainability, and reliability.
Stay abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in mechanical maintenance applying knowledge to drive continuous improvement initiatives.
Maintain documentation of maintenance activities, equipment specifications, manuals, and spare parts inventory, ensuring accuracy and accessibility for maintenance planning and decision-making.

Interactions: Works with hourly, salary and the management team.
Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related field.
1-3 years of experience in mechanical maintenance within an industrial manufacturing environment,
Good understanding of mechanical systems, equipment, and components commonly used in papermaking processes.
Leadership abilities with the ability to effectively manage and prioritize multiple tasks and projects.
Problem-solving skills and a systematic approach to troubleshooting mechanical issues.
Communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and organizational levels.
Knowledge of safety regulations and best practices in industrial maintenance. preferably in the pulp and paper industry.

 
Preferred Qualifications: Experience in the pulp and paper industry.

Position Summary:  
The Process Engineer is responsible for analysis, planning and control of the mechanical and chemical processes at the mill.  As a part of a continually improving plant, the Process Engineer is responsible for recommending design, operation, control and procedural improvements for a lower cost and higher quality end product. 
Dimensions:
PCA is the fourth largest manufacturer of containerboard and corrugates packaging in United States.  PCA is an ideas and solutions company.  We are a leader in helping our customer package, transport and display products of all kinds.  PCA embodies a culture of continuous improvement and, as such, is dedicated to delivering a high quality and sustainable product via innovative energy management and responsible design.  In 2014, our 6 containerboard plants (“Mills”) produced 3.5 million tons of containerboard netting $4.5 billion in sales to third parties. Each of PCAs containerboard plants house a stock pulp machine, Fourdrinier machine, ___ pressers, and myriad of other containerboard equipment.  In general, PCA strives for a maximum of ___ response time in case of an emergency stoppage.  The Process Engineer analyzes and plans the mechanical and chemical processes to improve mill profits and decrease the plants losses.
Principle Accountabilities:  

Improve the mill profit and loss statement by executing plans to design, conduct and evaluate trial work to advance the mill’s economic situation by continually improving safety, environmental, cost, quality, yield, productivity or compliance operations
Evaluate long-term compatibility of emerging technologies in the industry and make recommendations regarding equipment currently utilizes as well as purchasing new equipment
Investigate and solve production and process related problems by conducting studies, effluent treatment projects, and air quality studies, collecting data and conducting analysis to report back to manager with recommendations and conclusions 
Develops plans, specifications and reports for assigned trials 
Support peer engineers in conducting environmental, quality and productivity studies, analysis and process change.
Support the mills optimization/process control sustainability and continual improvement efforts by participating in environmental, quality, and productivity trials and assignments 
Investigate methods to decrease waste, productivity, and supply costs which improving quality and throughput
Work with senior engineers on complex assignments, assisting where necessary
Track initial base lines of the projects/controls and report out on savings
Communicate to staff how the actions of the Pulpmill/Power and Recovery departments controls impact customers
Train crew and management in all phases of plant operations


Knows and follows policies and procedures of the company shares information that would benefit other members of the team and finds ways to improve the delivery of service to our customers.
Strives to continually strengthen PCA’s business philosophy of meeting needs and exceeding expectation for customers.  This includes supporting PCA’s Commitment to Service which involves doing what’s right for our customers, focusing on strategies that add value and support growth, and keeping the promises that we make.

 
Decision Making: 
The Process Engineer is required to exercise discretion and creativity in determining best way optimize processes and addressing assignments.  The Process Engineer is expected to drive performance of the team assigned to his/her project to meet goals.  The Process Engineer is expected to take general directions and from those directions make decisions as to his/her approach to completing assigned projects and is expected determine how to operate and conduct assigned tasks within the established standards and procedures
 
 
Interactions with Customers and Contacts:           
Internally, the Process Engineer interacts with manufacturing and support personnel to complete assigned work.  Additionally, the Process Engineer is responsible for oversight and communication of pertinent improvement activities to manufacturing staff and management.  Externally, the Process Engineer has a network of field and process experts and is expected to grow and maintain those company contacts.  This position must also be able to develop contacts with new ideas/equipment and to be able to work with the mill and corporate staff to get those resources to the mill when needed.
Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemical Engineering or Paper Science and/or Engineering.
EIT certification or on EIT certification track preferred
2 years of work in a process engineering related role or equivalent. Paper mill experience or process knowledge preferred.
Must have good troubleshooting skills and knowledge of digital and analog control systems.
Ability to work with the required software for model based control applications.
Good written and verbal communication skills and ability to build and maintain positive relationships with team members.
Good organizational skills, decision maker and results oriented.
Ability to learn and develop Model Predictive Controls on all areas of responsibilities.
Self-starter, willing to work with minimal supervision and input from those who explain the needed results.
Ability to develop and train on processes and systems being put into place.
Demonstrated effective facilitation, project execution, and follow-up and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated track record of independent project leadership and value creation.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, Power Point, and Outlook required.
